title: Even-order Grünschloß–Keller permutation nets: net property and tiling distance
abstract: This Lean development proves that the even-order permutation construction of Grünschloß and Keller (MCQMC 2008 proceedings, implemented in gendiag0m2.h) is a base-2 (0,m,2)-net for every even m >= 4. The proof is symbolic: for every resolution a <= m the dyadic-box map is shown injective through the concatenation x = floor(k/4) + 2^(m/2-2) z and fixed-width bit-reversal splitting, and a cardinality argument upgrades injectivity to a bijection (exactly one point per elementary interval). For the source's row-shifted tiling lattice <(N,0),(N/4,N)> it proves, for every even m >= 8, that one explicit pair of points has squared distance 241 * 2^(m-8), and at m = 8 that 241 is the exact minimum over all pairs and all lattice translates. The exhaustive m = 8 lower bound is reduced by ordinary kernel decide; the exactness of the computed candidate minimum over the whole lattice is a symbolic lemma. The all-parameter lower bound of the distance theorem (even m >= 10) is proved in the paper but is not formalized.
